details:
**The Bund (Waitan)**
The waterfront promenade along Zhongshan Road on the west bank of the Huangpu River. It is lined with European-style banks and hotels built in the era of the foreign concessions and the International Settlement, and locals call it the Waitan ("outer bank").

**Pudong and Lujiazui**
Pudong is the district on the east bank of the Huangpu River, opposite the older city of Puxi. Its Lujiazui area, on a bend in the river, is Shanghai's financial center and holds most of the city's famous skyscrapers.

**Oriental Pearl Tower**
The TV tower in Lujiazui, Pudong, directly across the river from the Bund. Three columns support two large spheres stacked on top of each other, with a long antenna spire on top.

**Huangpu River**
The river that runs through Shanghai and divides Puxi from Pudong before joining the Yangtze River estuary. Bridges such as the Lupu Bridge cross it.

**Shanghai World Financial Center**
The skyscraper in Lujiazui nicknamed the "bottle opener" for the trapezoidal hole at its top. The original design used a circular hole, but it was changed after critics said it looked like the rising sun on the Japanese flag.

**Mouth of the Yangtze River**
Shanghai sits on the Yangtze River Delta at the river's mouth, downstream from Nanjing, between the Yangtze estuary and Hangzhou Bay to the south. It borders the provinces of Jiangsu and Zhejiang and is China's most populous city.

**Maglev and Pudong International Airport**
The Shanghai Maglev, the world's first commercial magnetic-levitation train line and among the fastest trains in the world, runs from Longyang Road Station to Pudong International Airport. The older Hongqiao Airport, on the west side of the city, also serves Shanghai.

**Mercedes-Benz Arena and Expo 2010**
Shanghai hosted the 2010 World Expo, and the Mercedes-Benz Arena was built as its performance venue. Denmark sent the original Little Mermaid statue from Copenhagen to its Expo pavilion, which was controversial at home.

**Jin Mao Tower**
An 88-story skyscraper in Lujiazui whose stepped design was inspired by traditional Chinese pagodas. It stands next to the World Financial Center and the Shanghai Tower.

**Yu Garden and the City God Temple**
The Yu Garden (Yuyuan) is a classical Ming-dynasty garden in the Old City. It is next to the Old City God Temple (Chenghuang Miao) and the busy bazaar around it.

**Nanjing Road and the Peace Hotel**
Nanjing Road is Shanghai's main shopping street, running west from the Bund. The Peace Hotel at its Bund end is the Art Deco Sassoon House built by Victor Sassoon. The Jing'an Temple stands on the western part of the road.

**Thames Town**
A planned town in the Songjiang district modeled on English market towns, with cobbled streets, Tudor-style buildings, and red phone booths. It was part of the "One City, Nine Towns" plan to build towns themed on foreign countries.

**Longtang and shikumen**
Longtang are the traditional lanes and alleys of residential Shanghai. They are lined with shikumen ("stone gate") townhouses, which mix Western terrace-house design with Chinese courtyard features.

**Xiaolongbao and Nanxiang**
Shanghai's famous soup dumplings, filled with meat and hot broth. They are closely linked with the Nanxiang Bun Shop near Yu Garden. Qibao Old Town, a preserved canal town crossed by the Puhui River, is another tourist spot in the city.

**Donghai Bridge and Yangshan Port**
The roughly 20-mile Donghai Bridge crosses Hangzhou Bay to link the mainland with the deep-water container port of Yangshan. That port is part of the Port of Shanghai, the busiest container port in the world.
